content.text: There is a strong presence of Ayurveda in Tamil Nadu. All over the state, 8 colleges exist that provide the BAMS admission in Tamil Nadu. Students who passed their 12th examination and have qualified for the NEET-UG can enrol themselves in the BAMS program in any of these colleges. But, you must need to attend the AYUSH counselling session in Tamil Nadu for BAMS Admission. The process is the same, just like the BAMS admission in India . In this article, we are going to discuss in detail the BAMS admission eligibility, fees, and top colleges in Tamil Nadu.

sections.heading: How to take BAMS Admission in Tamil Nadu

content.text: AYUSH counselling in Tamil Nadu is conducted by the counselling authority of the Directorate of Indian Medicine and Homoeopathy, Chennai. The National Eligibility cum Entrance Test is compulsory for all candidates who are considering to take BAMS admission in Tamil Nadu. After qualifying NEET UG examination, one must attend the counselling session for BAMS admission. There, the students are allotted their seats at the college based on their NEET rank, choice of colleges, and reservation. Out of 8 colleges, there is only one Government college, and the others are private ones. In total, 430 seats are available for BAMS admission in Tamil Nadu, and the Government college has 60 seats. The private colleges hold the rest 370 seats for admission.

sections.heading: BAMS Eligibility in Tamil Nadu

content.text: The eligibility criteria for the BAMS course are the same throughout India. The eligibility for BAMS admission in Tamil Nadu is as follows.

items: Students must appear in the NEET-UG examination and qualify with a minimum cutoff score.
Aspirants must have cleared Class 12 from a recognised board with subjects – Physics, Chemistry & Biology.
Students should have obtained a minimum percentage of 50% marks in the PCB subjects. For ST/SC and other reserved candidates, the minimum aggregate is 40%.
Students should be aged 17 years and above at the time of admission.

sections.heading: BAMS Admission Process in Tamil Nadu

content.text: The BAMS admission in Tamil Nadu is lengthy. Here we have provided a step-by-step guide for you. Follow these steps to complete the process successfully.
Step 1: First, appear in the NEET UG examination and score above the cut-off marks of that year to become eligible for BAMS admission.
Step 2: Register yourself on the Tamil Nadu state AYUSH counselling portal. The Directorate of Indian Medicine and Homoeopathy conducts the state counselling of Tamil Nadu.
Step 3: Upload and submit the necessary documents for admission. Upon submitting, a confirmation email will be sent to be registered email address.
Step 4: Attend the counselling, make your choice of the preferred colleges, and lock your choices.
Step 5: Depending on the NEET rank, candidates will be allotted BAMS seats according to their choices and seat availability in the colleges.
Step 6: Students must report to the colleges they are allotted. Remember to carry the required documents, both in originals and photocopies, and complete your document verification.
Step 7: Lastly, pay the required admission fees to confirm your seat allotment.

sections.heading: Documents Required for BAMS Admission

content.text: Aspiring students must submit the following list of documents at the time of registration. They must also bring these while reporting to the college. These documents are required both in originals and photocopies. Given below is the list of documents required for BAMS admission in Tamil Nadu.

items: AACCC Allocation letter
NEET Hall ticket
NEET Score Card
10th Marksheet & Certificate
12th Marksheet & Certificate
A document to prove the date of birth.
Transfer Certificate from the Institution last attended.
Migration Certificate from the Board/ University last attended.
A Character and Conduct Certificate from the Institution last attended.
Medical Fitness Certificate
Copy of Application form
Aadhar Card (Proof of identity)
Community Certificate in case of SC/ ST/OBC/OBC-EWS candidates.
Disability Certificate for Physically Handicapped Candidates (If applicable)
Photos – 6 Nos. Same as affixed in the application form

sections.heading: BAMS Course Fees in Tamil Nadu

content.text: The government of India and the Ministry of AYUSH have given the state governments independence to provide the BAMS course with their fee structure. So, the BAMS course fees in Tamil Nadu are different in several government and private colleges.

The government colleges have relatively lower course fees than the private ones. Although the private ones charge extra, they also promise the best infrastructure and well-trained faculty for the betterment of their peers. For getting the detailed fee structure, we recommend that the candidates visit the official website of the colleges or connect with us.

sections.heading: BAMS Careers in Tamil Nadu

content.text: There are plenty of BAMS jobs in Tamil Nadu. There are diverse career opportunities in both the public and private sectors. The graduates from the colleges have got the jobs of Ayurvedic Doctor, Medical Officer, Lecturer, or Scientist in different hospitals and nursing homes. The BAMS salary in Tamil Nadu ranges from INR 20,000/- to INR 50,000/- per month. Companies are seeking Clinical Practitioners, Healthcare Administrators, Researchers, and Wellness Operators for the Ayurvedic specialist, having the BAMS degree. Not only in Tamil Nadu, the BAMS graduates have a chance to establish themselves in different career paths all over India, and even in overseas countries.

sections.heading: Conclusion

content.text: For the medical aspirant students who recently passed their 12th, have another opportunity besides MBBS, BAMS – The Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery. sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
Who conducts BAMS counselling in Tamil Nadu?

content.text: The state AYUSH counselling is conducted by the Directorate of Indian Medicine and Homoeopathy.

sections.heading: What are the BAMS fees in Tamil Nadu?

content.text: As colleges decide the course fees, government and private colleges have different course fees. While in government colleges, the tuition fees stand between INR 20k to INR 50k annually, the private colleges charge between INR 1.5 to 5 lacs.

sections.heading: What is the BAMS eligibility in Tamil Nadu?

content.text: Eligibility for BAMS admission in Tamil Nadu is similar to the other states in India. Aspirants must pass the 12th with a 50% aggregate in Physics, Chemistry, and Biology/Biochemistry. Also should have to qualify NEET UG.

sections.heading: Is there any entrance test for BAMS admission in Tamil Nadu?

content.text: Yes, for BAMS admission in Tamil Nadu, all the students must qualify the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test. NEET UG is considered the sole entrance test for BAMS admission all over India.

sections.heading: Are there hostel facilities available in the BAMS college in Tamil Nadu?

content.text: Yes, both boys and girls hostels are available at the BAMS colleges in Tamil Nadu.

sections.heading: How many BAMS colleges are there in Tamil Nadu?

content.text: There are in total of 8 BAMS colleges in Tamil Nadu. Among them, one is a government institution and the others are private colleges.

sections.heading: How to get BAMS admission in Tamil Nadu?

content.text: After qualifying NEET UG, fill out the application form and submit it online on the website of the Directorate of Indian Medicine and Homoeopathy, and participate in the counselling for BAMS admission in Tamil Nadu.

sections.heading: How to apply for a BAMS course in Tamil Nadu?

content.text: Appear in NEET UG, then register and attend the AYUSH state counselling to apply for the BAMS course in Tamil Nadu.

sections.heading: What are the fees of a BAMS private college in Tamil Nadu?

content.text: The fees of a BAMS private college in Tamil Nadu range from INR 1.5 lacs to INR 3 lacs.
